result.stdout:
skail creates Skail projects from scratch, connects workers to an environment,
runs tasks and inspects them. Every command accepts --json and never prompts
without a terminal. Run `skail commands --json` for the machine-readable tree.

Usage:
  skail [command]

Available Commands:
  agents      Set up AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) for Skail
  billing     Plan and billing
  build       Build the workload (runs "build" from skail.json)
  commands    Describe every command, flag, exit code and output shape (for agents)
  completion  Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  debug       Replay a task locally, step by step (time travel)
  dev         Run the worker against the linked environment and show tasks as they happen
  doctor      Check login, project link, environment connection and whether a worker is running
  envs        Environments: where tasks run
  events      External events
  help        Help about any command
  init        Create a new Skail project from a template
  keys        Environment access keys
  link        Link the current folder to a project and environment
  login       Log in to Skail (device code in the browser, or a token from stdin)
  logout      Remove the stored credentials of this profile
  mcp         Run an MCP server (stdio) exposing the CLI as tools
  orgs        Organizations you belong to
  projects    Projects in the organization
  run         Start a task: call a function of a workload
  signup      Create a Skail account (opens the sign-up page; same flow as login)
  tasks       Inspect and operate task executions
  templates   Project templates
  up          Create or link everything skail.json needs, then write .env (idempotent)
  usage       Show the plan allowance used this cycle and when it runs out
  version     Print the CLI version
  whoami      Show the logged-in account, organization and role
  workloads   Workloads registered in the project

Flags:
      --api-url string   portal API base URL
      --debug            log HTTP requests
[truncated]
